import sys, json, re

# The fence the block contract asks for, and the one this cell shipped first.
# ```sidecar carries ONE object whose TOP-LEVEL KEYS are the sections; ```memory
# is the single-section form and is read as the section `memory`, so a colony
# that has not been rewired yet keeps writing (GH #605).
#
# The grammar is a 1:1 port of the harness parser
# (`workshop/evals/conversation-guide/run_guide.py`): the grammar that MEASURED
# the sidecar and the grammar that CUTS it in production have to be one grammar,
# or the adoption number stops speaking for the shipped lane.
FENCE = "```sidecar"
LEGACY_FENCE = "```memory"
LEGACY_SECTION = "memory"
# What makes a bare ```json fence or a naked trailing object an ATTEMPT rather
# than a code block. They are shapes of the legacy `memory` section: the cell
# judges no section here, it only recognises a wrapper the model missed.
LEGACY_MARKERS = ('"facts"', '"nothing_new"')

# SHORT IDS STAY INSIDE (GH #894, R-27-3: internal block ids never leave the
# colony). The curator shows the model every block of its window behind a short
# id, `[#<12 hex>]`, so that it can name one -- in a TRIM, in a history call. A
# model that has just read them quotes them in its prose as well, and prose is
# what a person, a chat window or another colony's agent reads. Every answer a
# model of this surface writes reaches its channel -- a peer colony's included --
# through this cell, so the id comes out here, deterministically and by form
# alone: a regular expression, never a judgement. What it does NOT touch: the
# sidecar block as the model wrote it (a TRIM names its ids there, and the
# curator reads them), a tool call's arguments (an id is exactly what a history
# tool takes), and the sections the composite names in `id_sections` -- the ones
# it routes to its own curator, which name ids on purpose. Every OTHER section
# leaves the composite toward a reader (a duplex voice speaks `fact`, `context`
# and `correction` aloud), so its strings are cleaned like prose (OR-KY-68).
# An id comes out in every form a model quotes one (OR-KY-80): the bracket of
# the window, the window's forms of a released, a shortened and an expired
# block (`curator/policy` RELEASED_FORM, SHRUNK_FORM, EXPIRED_FORM), the BARE
# `#<12 hex>` a history tool answers with, up to the sixteen digits it offers
# as `candidates` for an ambiguous id (OR-KY-81), and the full sixty-four-digit
# block id a `history_read` answer carries as `hash`, with or without `#`
# (OR-KY-84). Inside the window's own brackets any hex run is an id; standing
# on its own, a run is one only with a letter a-f in it and nothing word-like
# around it -- so a step number, a colour, an order number of digits, a hash of
# another length or a link fragment is no id. One expression, five more copies
# (collector digest, the core's question back, the curator's push and handover
# block), held byte for byte by a lock (OR-KY-83). Text without an id leaves
# byte for byte.
SHORT_ID = re.compile(
    r"[ \t]?(?:\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?: released[^\]\n]{0,64}| expired)?\]"
    r"|\[shortened[^\]\n#]{0,40}#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}[^\]\n]{0,4}\]"
    r"|\(#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}\)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#(?=[0-9]{0,15}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?!\w)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#?(?=[0-9]{0,63}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?!\w))")


def unmarked(text):
    """`text` without the short block ids it quotes; the same string when it
    quotes none. An id at the very start takes the space behind it along."""
    out = SHORT_ID.sub("", text)
    if out == text:
        return text
    return out.lstrip(" \t") if SHORT_ID.match(text) else out


def unmarked_turns(turns):
    """The turns a reader will see, their prose unmarked: text turns only,
    never a tool call; the same list when nothing changed."""
    out, changed = [], False
    for m in turns:
        if (isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("type") in ("text", None)
                and isinstance(m.get("text"), str)):
            text = unmarked(m["text"])
            if text != m["text"]:
                m = dict(m)
                m["text"] = text
                changed = True
        out.append(m)
    return out if changed else turns


def unmarked_payload(v):
    """A section's payload with every string in it unmarked, nested ones
    included -- values only, never a key (a key is the schema's name, not the
    model's words). Equal to what arrived when it quotes no id."""
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return unmarked(v)
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [unmarked_payload(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: unmarked_payload(x) for k, x in v.items()}
    return v


def fenced(text, low, fence):
    """The span a fence claims: `(raw, start, end)`, or `("", -1, -1)`."""
    at = low.find(fence)
    if at < 0:
        return "", -1, -1
    head = text.find("\n", at)
    close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
    if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
        return text[head + 1:close], at, close + 3
    # The opener is there and the closer is not: the completion stopped inside
    # the block. The whole tail from the fence is the attempt -- falling through
    # to the naked-object probe below would cut the JSON and leave the bare
    # fence line standing in the answer, which is the same leak one character
    # smaller (GH #534).
    return (text[head + 1:] if head >= 0 else ""), at, len(text)


def find_block(text):
    """The sidecar an answer carries: `found`, `legacy`, `raw`, `stripped`.

    NOTHING here repairs or re-serialises what the model wrote, and NOTHING here
    knows a section: a splitter that fixed a block would hand its readers its own
    repair instead of the model's, and one that judged a section by name would
    make every new section a change to this cell (GH #605). The only tolerance is
    on the FENCE, because decorating the wrapper is the failure mode
    format-restricted instructions actually show.

    `stripped` is computed whether or not the JSON in the middle parses, and that
    is the retraction GH #534 wrote here: `found` alone decides that the fence
    leaves the answer, because the cut is the span this function already located
    and the prose either side of it is the same prose either way.

    `span` is the block exactly as the model wrote it, fence included: the cut
    itself, handed on beside the answer so the model's own earlier answers can
    be shown to it WITH their block (GH #871).
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence, legacy in ((FENCE, False), (LEGACY_FENCE, True)):
        raw, start, end = fenced(text, low, fence)
        if start >= 0:
            return {"found": True, "legacy": legacy, "raw": raw,
                    "span": text[start:end],
                    "stripped": (text[:start] + text[end:]).strip()}
    # A bare ```/```json fence whose body carries a legacy payload counts as an
    # attempt: the model produced it and missed the label.
    for opener in ("```json", "```"):
        probe = 0
        while True:
            at = low.find(opener, probe)
            if at < 0:
                break
            head = text.find("\n", at)
            close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
            if head < 0 or close < 0:
                break
            body = text[head + 1:close]
            if any(m in body for m in LEGACY_MARKERS):
                return {"found": True, "legacy": True, "raw": body,
                        "span": text[at:close + 3],
                        "stripped": (text[:at] + text[close + 3:]).strip()}
            probe = close + 3
    # A naked object in the answer, same reasoning. Scanned from the LAST opening
    # brace backwards: the payload nests (`topic` is an object), so the last brace
    # in the text is an inner one and a lone rfind would never see a real payload
    # here.
    #
    # The attempt is the object that READS and holds the marker, not the first
    # brace whose tail holds one (fix strand F of GH #874, review minors of #871):
    # with `topic` written before `facts` that first brace is the inner `topic`,
    # read alone it has a brace too many, and the answer kept `{"topic":`. A
    # readable object is cut as the span it is, like a fence, so prose the model
    # wrote after it stays in the answer; only when nothing reads is the nearest
    # marker brace cut to the end -- a broken object says nowhere where it ends.
    brace = text.rfind("{")
    first = -1
    while brace >= 0:
        tail = text[brace:]
        if any(m in tail for m in LEGACY_MARKERS):
            outer = section_opening(text, brace)
            if outer >= 0:
                end = object_end(text, outer)
                if end < 0:
                    end = len(text)
                return {"found": True, "legacy": False, "raw": text[outer:end],
                        "span": text[outer:end],
                        "stripped": (text[:outer] + text[end:]).strip()}
            # The attempt holds the nearest marker brace: a readable object that
            # ends before it is an earlier one of the answer's own.
            end = object_end(text, brace)
            if (end > 0 and (first < 0 or end > first)
                    and any(m in text[brace:end] for m in LEGACY_MARKERS)):
                return {"found": True, "legacy": True, "raw": text[brace:end],
                        "span": text[brace:end],
                        "stripped": (text[:brace] + text[end:]).strip()}
            if first < 0:
                first = brace
        brace = text.rfind("{", 0, brace)
    if first >= 0:
        return {"found": True, "legacy": True, "raw": text[first:],
                "span": text[first:],
                "stripped": text[:first].strip()}
    return {"found": False, "legacy": False, "raw": "", "span": "", "stripped": text}


def object_end(text, at):
    """Where the JSON object opening at `at` ends, or -1 when none reads there."""
    try:
        doc, end = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text, at)
    except ValueError:
        return -1
    return end if isinstance(doc, dict) else -1


def section_opening(text, brace):
    """Where the OUTER object opens when the payload at `brace` is the value of
    the key `memory` -- the section form written without its fence -- or -1.

    GH #871 fix round 1: a model that drops the fence and keeps the section form
    writes `{"memory": {...}}`. The scan above meets the INNER object first; read
    alone it carries one closing brace too many, is flagged malformed, and the
    cut before it left `{"memory":` standing in the answer -- 26 of 26 channel
    answers in one harness run ended on it (the leak class of GH #534). The key
    right in front of the payload is what identifies the form; the object that
    opens it is the nearest brace behind the key whose tail reads as one object
    holding that key, and the nearest brace at all when none reads (a broken
    object is still cut whole, found decides the cut). The object is READ where
    it opens and not to the end of the answer, so prose after it does not hide
    it (fix strand F of GH #874)."""
    head = text[:brace].rstrip()
    key = '"%s"' % LEGACY_SECTION
    if not head.endswith(":") or not head[:-1].rstrip().endswith(key):
        return -1
    at = head[:-1].rstrip().rfind(key)
    first = text.rfind("{", 0, at)
    outer = first
    while outer >= 0:
        try:
            whole, end = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text, outer)
        except ValueError:
            whole, end = None, -1
        if isinstance(whole, dict) and LEGACY_SECTION in whole and end > brace:
            return outer
        outer = text.rfind("{", 0, outer)
    return first


doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
# The contract's own form of a turn that carried nothing, as ONE JSON object
# (GH #871 fix round 1). It is a knob and not a literal because this cell knows
# no section: the composite that wires the memory offer names the form, and a
# drift lock holds it to that offer's text. Empty, or not one object, means no
# block is shown beside a call -- the behaviour before the knob.
NOTHING_BLOCK = str((doc.get("params") or {}).get("nothing_block") or "").strip()
try:
    if not isinstance(json.loads(NOTHING_BLOCK or "null"), dict):
        NOTHING_BLOCK = ""
except ValueError:
    sys.stderr.write("splitter: nothing_block is not one JSON object -- ignored\n")
    NOTHING_BLOCK = ""
# The sections whose words keep their short block ids (GH #894): the composite
# names the ones it routes to its own curator, because this cell knows no
# section. An array or one comma-separated string; missing or empty, and every
# section is cleaned -- the safe side of R-27-3.
_ids = (doc.get("params") or {}).get("id_sections")
if isinstance(_ids, str):
    _ids = _ids.split(",")
ID_SECTIONS = {str(x).strip() for x in (_ids if isinstance(_ids, list) else [])
               if str(x or "").strip()}
h = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = dict(h.get("hop") or {})
msgs = d.get("messages") or []


def emit_pass_through(extra=None, raw=""):
    """Form 1: the turn travels on exactly as it arrived (`raw`: a block that
    rides beside it, GH #871)."""
    header = dict(hop)
    if extra:
        header.update(extra)
    out = {"header": header, "messages": unmarked_turns(msgs)}
    if raw:
        out["sidecar_raw"] = raw
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))


# A round with tool calls belongs to the dispatcher, whole. The splitter only
# ever touches a plain answer completion -- building the mixed form (text beside
# an async call in one message) is exactly the shape that strands a round
# (GH #378), and this is where we walk around it rather than into it.
if any(isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("type") == "tool_call" for m in msgs):
    # THE SENTENCE BESIDE THE CALLS STILL SHOWS A BLOCK (GH #871 fix round 1).
    # The round leaves untouched -- that stands -- but the text the model says
    # beside a call leaves through the dispatcher's interim path, the collector
    # files it like an answer, and on the consult's return it is an earlier
    # answer in the window. With no block it was the same precedent the #871
    # fix removed everywhere else: replayed (gpt-6-luna, 4 consult returns x 5),
    # the repaired window still showed that sentence bare, and the block stood
    # in 9 of 20 answers on a consult's return; with the contract's own nothing
    # form beside it, 19 of 20 (the arm that measured the form) and 14 of 20
    # (the replay of this cell as shipped). So such a sentence gets
    # that form as its `sidecar_raw` -- shown to the model, never to a reader,
    # and never on a section lane: nobody annotated this turn, and the memory
    # must not be told otherwise. A block the model DID write beside the call
    # stays where the model put it (the round is not cut, GH #378), so no second
    # one is laid over it.
    said = [m.get("text") for m in msgs if isinstance(m, dict)
            and m.get("type") in ("text", None) and isinstance(m.get("text"), str)
            and m.get("text")]
    if said and NOTHING_BLOCK and not any(find_block(t)["found"] for t in said):
        emit_pass_through(raw=FENCE + "\n" + NOTHING_BLOCK + "\n```")
    else:
        emit_pass_through()
    sys.exit(0)

# The LAST text turn that carries a block is the one that carries the sidecar:
# a model that quoted a fence earlier in the same completion did not annotate
# twice, it annotated at the end.
found_at, ann = -1, None
for i, m in enumerate(msgs):
    if not isinstance(m, dict):
        continue
    text = m.get("text")
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text:
        continue
    probe = find_block(text)
    if probe["found"]:
        found_at, ann = i, probe

if ann is None:
    emit_pass_through()
    sys.exit(0)

# Found decides the cut, readable decides the lane: the block comes out of the
# answer in every case from here on.
cleaned = list(msgs)
turn = dict(msgs[found_at])
turn["text"] = ann["stripped"]
cleaned[found_at] = turn
# The block is out; what is left is prose, and prose leaves without ids.
cleaned = unmarked_turns(cleaned)

try:
    parsed = json.loads(ann["raw"].strip())
except ValueError:
    parsed = None
if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
    parsed = None

if parsed is None:
    # The block is there and unreadable, and it STILL leaves the answer.
    #
    # RETRACTED (GH #534), because it was measured in a running colony: this
    # branch used to pass the answer through untouched, fence included, on the
    # reasoning that half-cutting a block nobody can read corrupts the answer
    # for the sake of a write that cannot happen anyway. A model dropped one
    # closing brace and a person read the JSON in their chat window. There is no
    # half cut to fear -- the span was already located, the prose either side of
    # it is the same prose -- so the only thing that branch bought was the leak.
    #
    # What does not change is the refusal to repair: nothing is re-serialised
    # and NOTHING goes out on `sidecar`, because there is nothing readable to
    # hand a reader. The flag stays, so the close pass can still tell "the model
    # missed the form" from "the model never annotated" and still owes the turn
    # an extraction.
    header = dict(hop)
    header["sidecar"] = "malformed"
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"header": header, "messages": cleaned}))
    sys.exit(0)

# One object, one message per top-level key. The cell distributes nothing and
# recognises nothing: `hop.section` is what the edges downstream read, so a
# section this tree has never heard of travels without a line of code here.
sections = {LEGACY_SECTION: parsed} if ann["legacy"] else parsed
out, dropped = [], []
for key, payload in sections.items():
    if key not in ID_SECTIONS:
        # A section that leaves toward a reader loses the short ids its words
        # quote, BEFORE the checks below: a bare string that was nothing but an
        # id is a section with no words (GH #894, OR-KY-68).
        payload = unmarked_payload(payload)
    if isinstance(payload, str):
        # A BARE STRING IS A SECTION BODY (GH #799, owner ruling R-L11 of
        # 2026-09-21). The two halves of the block contract asked for two
        # different things: the heading of a section is rendered out of the
        # schema whoever offered it wrote, and every section
        # `templates/talky/schemas/config.json` offers is a
        # `{"type": "string"}` -- so a model reading the heading writes
        # `{"fact": "<sentence>"}`, and until this line that section was
        # dropped. Measured on the twin at the consumer end of the same seam
        # (GH #797): thirteen delegations answered, zero paraphrases spoken.
        #
        # It is WRAPPED and NOT repaired, which keeps the promise one line
        # above: `payload` is the object slot this lane declares
        # (`contract.emits.body.payload`), and the string inside it is the one
        # the model wrote, byte for byte. The receiver reads it back out by
        # name, not by position (`crates/meclaw-cells/src/voice/cell.rs`,
        # `section_text`).
        if not payload.strip():
            # No words is no section, and the line is drawn where the RECEIVER
            # draws it: `words()` in the voice cell refuses a string whose
            # `trim()` is empty, so a key with nothing under it would buy the
            # lane an `error bad_section` instead of an advice.
            dropped.append(key)
            continue
        payload = {"payload": payload}
    elif not isinstance(payload, dict):
        # Neither an object nor a string. A list or a number under a top-level
        # key is a model that wrote past the form, and there is no body to
        # carry it in -- it is dropped with its name on the record rather than
        # guessed at.
        dropped.append(key)
        continue
    out.append({"header": {"route": "sidecar", "section": key},
                "messages": [], "section": key, "payload": payload})

# The reason the completion ended travels on (GH #843). Until 1.0.2 this was
# hard-coded to "stop", which was true while only `stop` reached this cell; a
# `length` finish now comes through here too, so its sidecar is cut by the one
# grammar that cuts it, and the collector stamps `truncated` off this key.
answer = {"finish_reason": str(hop.get("finish_reason") or "stop")}
if dropped:
    answer["sidecar_dropped"] = ",".join(dropped)
# The block rides on the answer half as its own body slot (GH #871), because the
# window is built from what this half leaves behind: the collector files the
# answer text as `content` and, until 1.0.3, nothing else -- so every earlier
# answer the model was shown stood there WITHOUT its block. Replayed against the
# turns of a running colony (gpt-6-luna, 23 turns x 5): with that window the
# model wrote the block in 38 % of the turns that had an earlier answer in
# view; with the same window showing each earlier answer with its block, 98 %.
# Only a READABLE block rides: a malformed one is a precedent nobody should be
# shown. It is the model's own span, byte for byte -- nothing here re-serialises
# it -- and it never reaches a channel: the collector stores it and hands the
# answer on with `messages` only.
half = {"header": answer, "messages": cleaned, "sidecar_raw": ann["span"]}
emitted = [half] + out
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(emitted if len(emitted) > 1 else emitted[0]))

nothing_block.description: GH #871 fix round 1: the contract's form of a turn that carried nothing, as ONE JSON object. A tool round whose text carries no block leaves untouched with this object, fenced as ```sidecar, on `sidecar_raw`, so the sentence said beside the calls shows the model a block when it stands in a later window. Shown to the model only: it never reaches a section lane or a channel. Set to the memory hive's nothing form; a drift lock holds the two together. Empty, or not one object, shows nothing.

id_sections.description: GH #894 (R-27-3, OR-KY-68): the sections whose words keep the curator's short block ids `[#<12 hex>]` -- the ones the composite routes to its own curator, which name ids on purpose (`window` releases and pins them). Every other section leaves toward a reader and every string in it loses its ids, as the prose does. An array or one comma-separated string. Shipped as the three the talky routes to its curator; a params block that leaves it out or empties it cleans EVERY section (the safe side of R-27-3). This cell judges no section by name: the list is the composite's statement, held to its `./splitter -> ./curator` edge by a drift lock.

sidecar_raw.description: GH #871: on the answer half, the block exactly as the model wrote it (fence included) when it was readable; on a tool round whose text carries no block, the contract's nothing form out of `nothing_block`, fenced (fix round 1). The collector stores it beside the answer and shows it with that answer in the next windows; no channel receives it.

finish_reason.description: How the completion ended. Passed through onto the answer half of a cut since 1.0.2 (GH #843), `stop` when the hop carries none -- until then the cut answer claimed `stop` whatever arrived, which was only true while nothing else reached this cell.

description.purpose: The seam that takes the sidecar back out of an answer, and it knows no section. A brain completion arrives on the answer path; if its text carries a fenced `sidecar` block, ONE JSON object is read out of it and ONE MESSAGE PER TOP-LEVEL KEY leaves on route `sidecar` with `hop.section` set to that key, beside the answer with the block cut out. A section's body is either an OBJECT, handed on exactly as the model wrote it, or a BARE NON-EMPTY STRING, wrapped as `{"payload": "<string>"}` -- the string is the form the offers ask for and the wrapper is the body slot this lane declares (GH #799). The legacy single-section fence `memory` is still read and becomes the section `memory`, so a colony that has not been rewired keeps writing. Without a block contract in the brain's instructions there is nothing to find and this cell is a pure pass-through. Since GH #894 it also takes the curator's short block ids `[#<12 hex>]` out of what it hands on toward a reader -- the prose of every text turn, and every string of a section the composite does not name in `id_sections` -- because every answer a model of this surface writes reaches its channel through this cell, a peer colony's included (R-27-3: internal block ids never leave the colony). The block as written, a tool call's arguments and the sections routed to the curator keep their ids; text that quotes none leaves byte for byte. The one reader-bound text that does not come through here, the digest of a capped round, is the collector's own and it cleans that itself.
description.use_when: Inside the talky composite, on the brain's answer path only -- between ./brain and ./dispatcher -- and, since 1.0.2, between ./brain and ./collector for a completion cut on `length` (GH #843), so a cut answer loses its sidecar the same way a finished one does. The parent MUST wire the `sidecar` port out of the composite and distribute it on `hop.section`, or every section dead-letters while the answers keep going out fine, which is the failure nobody sees.
description.not_in_scope: No repair, no re-serialisation, no receiver knowledge. The cell never judges a section by name: what a section means belongs to whoever declared it, and a splitter that knew the names would need changing for every new one. The one list of names it reads, `id_sections` (GH #894), is the composite's statement which sections keep their short block ids, not this cell's. A block that does not parse, or whose top level is not an object, is CUT out of the answer like any other and then dropped -- only the flag travels, and nothing unreadable is handed on, because a repaired block would be this cell's invention rather than the model's. RETRACTED in GH #534: until then such a block was left INSIDE the answer, and a model that dropped one closing brace put raw JSON in front of a person. Found decides the cut; readable decides the lane. A section whose value is neither an object nor a non-empty string -- a list, a number, an empty string -- is dropped by name rather than guessed at. WRAPPING a bare string (GH #799) is not a repair and is the one shape this cell adds: the string travels byte for byte, in the object slot the lane declares, because the offers every section is written from promise a string and the heading a model reads shows one. The empty string is refused HERE because the receiver refuses it there: a section with no words is an `error bad_section` at the far end, so it never leaves as an advice. No tool-call round is ever touched: a completion carrying calls belongs to the dispatcher whole, because the mixed form -- text beside an async call in one message -- is the shape that strands a round (GH #378) and this cell exists to walk around it. What such a round MAY carry since GH #871 fix round 1 is one extra body slot: `sidecar_raw` with the contract's nothing form (`nothing_block`), when its text carries no block -- the calls themselves are still handed on byte for byte, and the sentence beside them loses only the short block ids it quotes (GH #894).
description.emits_meaning: route sidecar: one message per section the block carried, `hop.section` naming it, body `{messages: [], section, payload}` -- the payload is the section as the model wrote it, parsed and not otherwise touched but for the short block ids (`[#<12 hex>]`, the bare `#` and twelve to sixteen hex digits or the full sixty-four-digit block id of a history tool's answer and the window's forms of a released, shortened or expired block -- OR-KY-80), which leave every string of a section `id_sections` does not name (GH #894) -- an object verbatim, a bare non-empty string wrapped once as `{"payload": "<string>"}` so it rides the object slot the body declares (GH #799). On the answer half: the finish_reason the completion arrived with (`stop` when it carried none; `length` for a cut one since 1.0.2, GH #843), and the same turns minus the fence and minus the short block ids their prose quotes (GH #894); `sidecar_dropped` lists the sections that could carry nothing -- neither an object nor a non-empty string -- comma-separated, in the order the model wrote them. sidecar malformed on a single message: a block was there and could not be read, so it was cut out of the answer and went nowhere -- the reader never sees a fence this cell found, and the close pass still owes the turn an extraction (GH #534).
description.consumes_meaning: the brain's completion on stop, tool_calls or -- since 1.0.2 -- length (messages plus the hop it arrived with). The fence grammar is a 1:1 port of the harness parser that measured the adoption of this form (```sidecar, the legacy ```memory, plus a tolerance for a bare ```json fence or a naked trailing object carrying the legacy payload): the grammar that measured it and the grammar that cuts it are one grammar.
examples: answer + ```sidecar block with two sections -> three messages: prose to the dispatcher, one message per section on route sidecar
answer + ```sidecar block `{"fact": "Der Termin ist Dienstag."}` -> two messages: the prose, and the section `fact` with payload `{"payload": "Der Termin ist Dienstag."}`
a section whose value is `""` or a list -> dropped by name in `sidecar_dropped`, the readable sections beside it travel
answer + legacy ```memory block -> two messages: prose to the dispatcher, the block as section memory
answer with no block -> one message, byte-identical (a colony without the block contract)

tool-call round -> one message, its calls byte-identical, block or no block (the sentence beside them loses only a short block id it quotes, GH #894); if its text carries no block, `sidecar_raw` is the fenced `nothing_block` (GH #871)

answer quoting `[#0123456789ab]` beside a block `{"fact": "See [#0123456789ab].", "window": {"release": ["#0123456789ab"]}}` -> the prose and the `fact` payload without the id; `window` (named in `id_sections`) keeps it (GH #894)
